applied.quote:
A robo-advisor fits a reader who wants low-cost automated investing for a defined goal and accepts little human contact, while a human adviser fits a reader who needs advice beyond investing or wants a person to call. When the human professional is a registered investment adviser, the duty of care and loyalty matches what an automated robo-adviser owes under federal law. If that professional operates as a broker or dual registrant, a different legal standard may govern transactions, as outlined in Form CRS. This assessment changes if an automated platform provides hybrid human consultation at your account balance, or if a prospective human adviser operates under a broker-only registration.

Take action by examining public regulatory disclosures before opening an account with any firm. Search the firm and individual professional on the SEC [IAPD](https://adviserinfo.sec.gov) website to review their Form ADV Part 2 narrative brochure and Form CRS relationship summary. Compare total all-in costs, including advisory fees, fund expenses, and platform charges, and verify the exact scope of human communication provided in your written advisory contract.
